title: The Crows in the Kingdom
summary: Akbar asks his ministers to count all the crows in Agra, threatening punishment if they fail. Birbal provides an ingenious answer that no one can disprove.
full_text:
On a breezy summer morning, Emperor Akbar stood with Birbal upon the marble terrace of the Agra Fort, gazing out over the sprawling city, the glittering Yamuna, and the flock of crows wheeling in the pale sky. In a playful mood, the Emperor decided to test his courtiers' wits with an impossible puzzle.

Turning to his assembled ministers, Akbar commanded, 'Tell me at once—how many crows reside within the borders of my capital city of Agra? I want an exact count by sunset, or each of you shall forfeit a week's allowance!'

The courtiers looked at one another in sheer terror. Counting crows was madness! They flitted from rooftop to minaret, roosted in trees, and flew across riverbanks without pause. While the other nobles whispered anxiously and wrung their hands, Birbal stood quietly, smiling with gentle amusement.

'Well, Birbal,' Akbar demanded, 'do you know the answer, or does your wisdom fail before common birds?'

Birbal bowed low with folded hands. 'Sire, the count is simple. There are exactly fifty-two thousand, four hundred and sixty-three crows in the city of Agra.'

Akbar raised his eyebrows in astonishment. 'Are you certain of this figure, Birbal? What if my royal inspectors count them and find a different number?'

'Your Majesty,' Birbal replied without a heartbeat's hesitation, 'if your guards find more crows than my number, it simply means their relatives from neighboring kingdoms have come to visit them in Agra for the summer holidays. And if they find fewer, it means that some of our Agra crows have flown away to visit their cousins in Delhi or Lahore!'

A burst of hearty laughter broke from Emperor Akbar's chest. Delighted by Birbal's unassailable presence of mind, he rewarded him with a string of lustrous pearls, remarking that wit can illuminate even the most absurd corners of life.
